name: wgmma_overlap
supersedes: nothing (v5 rules stay installed); adds cells
mechanisms: hopper.wgmma.register_file_issue_steal (kind 44, C3 + C7 + R as installed)
instruction.service units of MUFU / FMNMX / FADD / FFMA with several warps per SMSP

devices.h100: sm_90a pod (own quota of the fg-cold line)

question: With two or three warps per SMSP running a softmax-like FP32 stream (independent MUFU.EX2, FFMA with a reusable operand pair, a dependent FMNMX chain, a dependent FADD chain) while wgmma ops execute on the SM -- issued by the window warps' own warpgroup (self) or by another warpgroup (other) -- how much SMSP time does one stream instruction take?
why: fa3_fwd_hdim_small_05 on main 8c848cb5 (sim / ncu 0.78; $A/fg-line-cold/attrib1, attrib2; tools region_visits.py, warp_trace.py): per consumer warp and iteration the hardware spends 1869 cycles in the softmax loop (391 issues) and 395 at the wait for the QK wgmma, the simulation 982 and 1025; everything else agrees within about 10 %. In the simulation the three consumer warps of an SMSP run their softmax one after another (2.2 cycles of SMSP time per softmax issue, the tensor pipe is busy all the time); on hardware the visits overlap and one softmax issue takes 2.9 cycles of SMSP time. fp32_mix and fp_stream_mix reproduce such mixes without a wgmma (W >= 2 within 6 %); wgmma_overlap r7 has no softmax mix, no dependent FMNMX / FADD chain and no W = 3 cell (other.w2 = ctrl for independent kinds, dep3r 4.5-5.0 against 3.98).
probe: probe/overlap_v4.cu = overlap_v3.cu plus W = 3 and two window kinds. smx (unit I, I % 5): 0 ex2.approx.ftz on d[(I / 5) & 3]; 1 fma.rn d[4] = d[4] * a + b; 2 fma.rn d[5] = d[5] * a + b (a, b the reusable pair); 3 max.NaN d[6] = max(d[6], c[I & 3]); 4 add d[7] = d[7] + c[I & 3]. smxc: the same with unit 0 replaced by fma.rn d[(I / 5) & 3] = d * a8[k] + b8[k]. U = 140, G = 16 ops in flight, forms hgmma_bf16_n128_ss and hgmma_bf16_n256_rs, modes ctrl.w1-3, self.w1-3, other.w2-3; --launches 8 --reps 33, two runs; per-warp rows as v3 (the warps of warpgroup 0 are the owners of the ops in self mode).

prediction_of_the_installed_rules (cycle.ctrl: smx 1.9 / 3.1 / 4.9 at W = 1 / 2 / 3 (the fp_stream_mix mix5 hardware values; same mix with an FADD chain instead of a third FFMA); smxc about 1.6 x W below 2 warps of issue-slot bound.
prediction_of_the_installed_rules (cycle.other: window warps of other warpgroups do not pay for independent instructions (r7), the chains are not binding at 5 instructions per step: other.w2 = ctrl.w1 (1.9), other.w3 = ctrl.w2 (3.1).
prediction_of_the_installed_rules (cycle.self: the owners' warps pay the floor max(stall, 2, n_GPR), 4 for instructions that carry a reuse flag, +0.5 for the rs form: with the two FFMA flagged, mean floor 2.8 (ss) / 3.3 (rs) per instruction for the owner warp at W = 1; at W = 2 / 3 the non-owner warps run as in ctrl with one fewer competitor.

reading.usable: runs within 3 %; overlap gate as v3 (ops still executing at the end of the window; cells that fail are dropped and listed); SASS window = 140 instructions of the declared classes, reuse flags of the FFMA recorded.
reading.SMSP time: per cell, s = 1 / sum over the window warps of one SMSP of (1 / t_warp) = SMSP cycles per stream instruction.
reading.R1: other.w3 and self.w3 within max(15 %, 0.3) of the prediction and s <= 2.2 -> the installed rules cover this stream; the flash-attention softmax cost (2.9) is not reproduced by a probe and stays a kernel-level open item (reported with the phase analysis).
reading.R2: s >= 2.6 in other.w3 or self.w3, or a miss beyond the tolerance -> the excess is in the probe; the table by mode / W / form is the result and a rule is proposed in an addendum (post hoc) and judged on cells its constants do not come from.

not_allowed: no value chosen by full-GPU error; no rule per kernel; criteria changed only by an addendum stating why and whether data had been seen.

reading_of_run_4.limit counts commit groups: owner alone, n128: with one commit group per op the issue takes 391 / 1159 cycles for G = 12 / 24 (as run 3); with a commit after every third or sixth op it takes 251.5 / 491.5 = 21 per op, not held. The 'six pending ops' of addendum 3 is six pending commit groups. The rule installed after run 3 (Q on ops) is therefore wrong for sections that put several ops into one group -- the flash-attention sections (6 + 9 ops in two groups) are never held at launch on hardware, and the full-GPU movement of that family came from a condition that does not occur there.

run_9 (mode grpq).kernel: k_grpq<CID, SHAPE>: launch bound 384 threads; EVERY thread executes the ops (no predicate around them); the number of issuing warpgroups is the block size of the launch (128 / 256 / 384), so all cells of a shape execute the same SASS.
